clue.text: It probably entails an evening out

definitions.text: It probably entails an evening out

parts.words: It probably entails an evening out
parts.note: reads like a night on the town, but evening out means things balancing up over many trials, the principle that luck even itself out

explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'I;' is a misprint of 'It'. 'An evening out' suggests a date or party; here it is the levelling of results over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular principle says chance results tend to balance in the long run, an evening-out of good and bad luck.

clue.text: Excessive guidance for first group of players

definitions.meaning: the reins once used to steer toddlers, hence overbearing control
taken whimsically as the lead section of an orchestra's string players

explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in reins like a toddler means smothering control; and the leading strings of an orchestra would be its first violins.

clue.text: Former advisory group I want reconstituted

indicators.note: reconstituted means the letters of I want are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wants an old council brought back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: The witan was the council of nobles and clerics who advised Anglo-Saxon kings.

clue.text: Excitement produced by fellow always on the wicket

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
in cricket the wicket is the strip of ground between the stumps, also called the pitch

explanation.surface: A cricket fan's thrill at a player who is always out on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the wicket and the pitch both name the prepared strip the ball is bowled on.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is a state of intense agitation or excitement, as among a crowd.

clue.text: Regarding travel document that's almost duplicated

indicators.note: almost means the doubled word stops short of its final letter
duplicated says the document's word is written twice over

parts.note: a visa is the stamp or permit needed to enter a country

explanation.surface: A clerk queries a travel document that seems to have been nearly copied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplicated' gives VISAVISA, and 'almost' drops the last A.
explanation.definitionFit: Vis-a-vis is French for face to face, used in English to mean in relation to or concerning.

clue.text: It's only just, if this criminal gets a hearing

definitions.text: It's only just, if this criminal gets a hearing

parts.words: It's only just, if this criminal gets a hearing
parts.note: sounds like a plea for a fair trial, but the hearing meant is the soft sound a stealthy thief makes, only just audible

explanation.walkthrough: 'just' and 'hearing' suggest justice and a court; really a faint noise is only just heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief steals livestock, and the verb from which his name comes also means to make a soft swishing noise.

clue.text: American serving needs way to get point

parts.note: a GI is an American serviceman
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An American soldier needs a route to reach his objective.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of an argument is its essential meaning, its main point.

clue.text: Bullet, see, could be this colour

indicators.note: could be says the letters of bullet see may be reworked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Look, a bullet might have this metallic hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel blue is a dark greyish blue, the shade of tempered steel and gun metal.

clue.text: Left-winger's performance added point to big game

parts.note: a match between national teams is an international
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A socialist's show added a point in a big international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big game' suggests hunting; it is a match between countries. The definition is the socialist anthem as performed.
explanation.definitionFit: The anthem of the socialist and communist movement is sung by those on the political left.

clue.text: Start of play — scenes lacking a militant group

parts.note: the start of a play is Act I, its first act

indicators.note: lacking says the word for scenes goes without the letter a

parts.note: scenes or views are vistas
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre note: the opening act cut its scenes, leaving a band of militants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of play' reads as an opening; in crosswords it is ACT I, the first act. 'lacking' drops the A from the scenes word.
explanation.definitionFit: Activists are campaigners who take vigorous, often confrontational action, so as a body they form a militant group.

clue.text: Some birds in flight fell-about a quarter

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other, the hide wrapping the compass point

parts.note: fell as a noun is an animal's hide or skin
east is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Some birds in flight fell, about a quarter of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb about birds dropping; it is the noun meaning a hide. A compass point is a quarter in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the word for a flock of wild geese or ducks flying in formation.

clue.text: Private's not a particularly good shot

definitions.meaning: private in the sense of inward, personal, not shown outside
on an archery or rifle target the ring just outside the bull scores less than a bullseye

explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private ones; and the inner is the target ring next to the bull, a decent but not top-scoring hit.

clue.text: Animal not missing a trick

definitions.meaning: a small rodent like a field mouse
in some card games, winning every trick in a deal is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The vole is a small rodent; in card games such as ecarte a vole is a sweep of all the tricks.

clue.text: Fruit that's late, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for late is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a late train or clock is slow

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit that seems to be running behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small sour blue-black fruit of the blackthorn, used in sloe gin.

clue.text: Much too far beyond the trenches

definitions.meaning: soldiers in the First World War climbing out of their trench to attack

explanation.definitionFit: Going too far is being excessive; in trench warfare, going over the parapet meant leaving the trench to attack.

clue.text: Defensive players ior game left out of combined sides

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game of stones

indicators.note: out of says the abbreviation for left is taken from the word for combined sides

parts.note: sides that join forces are allies

explanation.surface: A team picks its defenders for a match, leaving someone out of a combined side.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'ior' is a misprint of 'for', a link word. 'out of' drops just one L from the combined sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalkeepers are the last line of defence in football or hockey, so they are defensive players.

clue.text: A gruesome end avoided on continent for this aristocrat?

indicators.note: end avoided says the word for gruesome loses its last letter

parts.note: nasty means gruesome or horrid
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A grand duchess said to have escaped a grisly fate abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end avoided' cuts NASTY to NAST. The question mark points to the Russian grand duchess rumoured to have survived her family's murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Duchess Anastasia, daughter of the last Tsar, was a Romanov princess.

clue.text: It helps to protect position composer's occupying

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero
occupying a place means being in it

explanation.surface: A guard post that a composer has taken over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' belongs to the definition: it is a military position the work protects.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravelin is a triangular outwork built in front of a fortress wall to shield it from attack.

clue.text: Managed to get 100 in the partial issue of shares

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the word the, splitting it

parts.note: taken as written
ran a business means managed it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A firm managed to raise a hundred in a share issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed to get 100' reads like a batsman's century, but C is the Roman hundred and 'in' places both pieces inside THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a slice or instalment, especially one portion of a larger issue of stock.

clue.text: Corruption of vice den made clear

indicators.note: corruption suggests the letters of vice den are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: The depravity of a den of vice was exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to show it plainly, so evinced means displayed or revealed.

clue.text: Constable's superior, it's said, as a painter

indicators.note: it's said says the police rank is spoken and heard, not written

parts.note: a police constable answers to the next rank up, a sergeant

explanation.surface: Someone senior to Constable, it's claimed, as an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was a famous English painter, so 'Constable's superior' tempts an art comparison; it is the police rank. John Singer Sargent was an American portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a celebrated portrait artist of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: Belgian writer's name concealed by patriarch

indicators.note: concealed by says the abbreviation is held hidden inside the patriarch's name

parts.note: Simeon was a son of Jacob, a biblical patriarch

explanation.surface: A Belgian author has a name kept secret by a church elder.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'writer's' is 'has', a link. Georges Simenon created the detective Maigret.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the prolific Belgian novelist behind Inspector Maigret.

clue.text: Absorbed by piece of thin towel

indicators.note: piece of says the letters are a run lifted from inside the words thin towel

explanation.surface: Soaked up by a scrap of thin towel.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absorbed by a hobby is to be keen on it, as in being very keen on jazz.

clue.text: House and stable

explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a company, as in a publishing house; and a firm footing is a steady, secure one.

clue.text: Animal having sort of bath by the river

parts.note: a hip bath is a small bath one sits in up to the hips
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A creature that likes bathing beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for hippopotamus, the large African mammal that wallows in rivers.

clue.text: Minimal amount of money put on 21's horse

parts.note: p, a penny, is the smallest unit of British money
21 refers to the answer of clue 21 across, defined there as absorbed by

explanation.surface: A small bet placed on someone's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' only joins the pieces. A pinto is a piebald horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a horse with patchy markings of white and another colour, popular in the American West.

clue.text: Necklace in either end of chest

annotationWithheld.why: Necklace in either end of chest (4): reads as T OR C, so 'end of chest' must give both T and C, one phrase doing two jobs, which the grammar refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: Necklace in either end of chest

clue.text: New gadget, in practice, has to operate outside

indicators.note: outside puts the word for operate round the word for practice

parts.note: a machine that operates or works is said to go
an ism is a practice or doctrine, as in a distinctive system

explanation.surface: A new gizmo has to be put into practice and made to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in practice' looks like a phrase meaning 'actually', and 'outside' is the container signal; 'in' and 'has to' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is any clever little device or contraption, often a novel one.

clue.text: Read some poetry for an Italian girl

parts.note: to con a text is to study or read it carefully
a stanza is a group of lines, a portion of a poem

explanation.surface: Reading out a verse for a young Italian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed answer CONSTANTA does not fit the wordplay: STANZA, a verse, ends ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Constanza is an Italian feminine given name, a form of Constance.

clue.text: For such a person, one can predict upsets

definitions.text: For such a person, one can predict upsets

indicators.note: upsets as a verb means the letters of one can predict are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people are so clumsy that mishaps can be forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: upsets are what you can predict for a clumsy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who regularly has mishaps is clumsy, so mishaps around them are foreseeable.
